rv.q: There's a lot of deep trauma happening all at once in this well-made play and you see some of the unspooling plot revelations coming.
For the audience, it’s a place where the fallout from the longest war in U.S. history transpires with a force that makes for gripping theater and enduring impact.
Altogether, Northlight has mounted a moving production of SELLING KABUL worthy of the play's many accolades.
Khoury’s script is nothing short of suspenseful perfection.
This play will rock you to your core.
A phenomenal cast and brilliantly clever script make Selling Kabul an emotional roller coaster from start to finish.
How or if people are rescued, and what decisions need to be made at the time, make for powerful and heartrending drama.
The tension slowly but surely ratchets up to the point where a character’s muffled scream into a pillow is deafening.
Selling Kabul's compelling and spine-tingling narrative provides an up-close, intense, and enthralling story of a sister's tested yet unyielding love, her brother, who the Tailban is pursuing.

Peck, Kamal and Vossoughi play out their deadly game of chess in such a way that we see there are no heroes and villains here, only victims doing anything they can to protect themselves and the ones they love.
Every aspect of this production is exquisite.

The lighting (Maximo Grano de Oro) and sound ( Jeffrey Levin) are right on making this 90 wonderful minutes of storytelling that will capture the hearts of anyone who has ever been involved in a war or battle.

cn.t: Critics praise this Pulitzer finalist as a gripping, suspenseful thriller that explores loyalty and sacrifice with Hitchcockian intensity. Khoury's taut drama about Afghanistan's aftermath strikes nerves with its emotional power and meticulous storytelling.
